approaches.name: Anterior hip approach (Smith-Petersen)
approaches.corridor: Superficial interval between sartorius and tensor fasciae latae; deep interval between rectus femoris and gluteus medius

procedure_applications.condition: Anterior exposure selected and surgeon experienced with the approach
Open reduction or anterior capsular access is required

positioning.text: Position the patient supine on a radiolucent table; the setup should permit imaging and manipulation of the operative leg.

setup.text: Prep and drape the limb so traction, rotation, and distal extension of the exposure remain possible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the anterior superior iliac spine and the course of the tensor fasciae latae before incision.

incision.text: Begin just distal and lateral to the anterior superior iliac spine and extend distally in line with the tensor fasciae latae.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the internervous interval between sartorius (femoral nerve) medially and tensor fasciae latae (superior gluteal nerve) laterally.

deep_interval.text: Continue between rectus femoris medially and gluteus medius laterally to reach the anterior capsule.

layers.text: Skin and subcutaneous tissue, tensor fascia, sartorius–tensor interval, rectus–gluteus interval, then anterior hip capsule.

structures_encountered.text: The ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery crosses the deep dissection and may require controlled ligation or coagulation.

structures_at_risk.text: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is vulnerable near the anterior superior iliac spine and medial edge of the tensor fasciae latae.
The femoral nerve and vessels are endangered by deep or medially directed instrumentation and retractors.

danger_zones.text: Keep the initial fascial opening lateral and protect the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve by avoiding aggressive medial subcutaneous dissection.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid placing sharp retractors intracapsularly along the superolateral femoral neck, where they may threaten retinacular blood supply to the femoral head.

exposure.text: Provides direct anterior access to the hip capsule, femoral head and neck, and adjacent ilium; distal extension can increase access to the proximal femur.

limitations.text: Femoral exposure and instrumentation can be demanding; fracture fixation may require an additional lateral incision or extension.

extensions.text: Proximal extension follows the iliac crest; distal extension continues along the anterolateral thigh while preserving the relevant neurovascular structures.

indications.text: Useful for anterior hip arthroplasty, open reduction requiring anterior capsular access, biopsy, drainage, and selected reconstructive procedures.

relative_contraindications.text: Use caution when required exposure or fixation cannot be achieved through the anterior corridor without unsafe traction or an unplanned second window.

implant_implications.text: Plan a separate lateral window when the selected proximal-femoral implant cannot be inserted safely through the anterior exposure.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Supine positioning facilitates AP and lateral fluoroscopic assessment, but the drape and table must preserve unobstructed image access.

closure.text: Repair the capsule when indicated, restore any released rectus origin, and close tensor fascia without entrapping the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.

complications.text: Approach-specific problems include lateral femoral cutaneous neuropraxia, femoral neurovascular injury, bleeding from lateral femoral circumflex branches, and inadequate femoral exposure.

bailouts.text: If femoral or implant access remains unsafe, stop forceful retraction and extend the exposure or add the planned lateral window.

questions.question: What is the superficial internervous plane in the Smith-Petersen approach?
questions.answer: Sartorius medially and tensor fasciae latae laterally.

approaches.name: Anterolateral hip approach (Watson-Jones)
approaches.corridor: Interval between tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly

procedure_applications.condition: Open reduction and lateral proximal-femoral fixation are required

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral according to the planned procedure, with the greater trochanter and anterior superior iliac spine accessible.

setup.text: Drape to permit hip motion and distal extension along the lateral femur when fixation is planned.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the anterior superior iliac spine, greater trochanter, and femoral shaft.

incision.text: Center the incision over the anterolateral greater trochanter, extending proximally toward the anterior superior iliac spine and distally along the femur as needed.

superficial_interval.text: Open fascia lata and develop the interval between tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly.

deep_interval.text: Expose the anterior capsule while protecting the abductors; limited release of anterior vastus lateralis or abductor insertion may be required by the procedure.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, tensor–gluteus medius interval, pericapsular tissue, then anterior hip capsule.

structures_encountered.text: Branches of the lateral femoral circumflex system may cross the interval and should be controlled deliberately.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve and vessels limit proximal dissection, and femoral neurovascular structures are at risk from anterior retractor placement.

danger_zones.text: Do not extend the gluteus medius dissection proximally without accounting for the superior gluteal neurovascular bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep anterior retractors on bone and avoid deep medial placement toward the femoral nerve and vessels.

exposure.text: Provides access to the anterior hip capsule, acetabular rim, femoral neck, and lateral proximal femur.

limitations.text: Posterior acetabular access is limited, and aggressive abductor release can compromise postoperative abductor function.

extensions.text: Extend distally by elevating the anterior vastus lateralis to accommodate lateral proximal-femoral implants.

indications.text: Applicable to total hip arthroplasty, hemiarthroplasty, selected femoral-neck fracture procedures, and proximal-femoral exposure.

relative_contraindications.text: Consider another exposure when extensive posterior acetabular visualization or a broader femoral corridor is required.

implant_implications.text: Lateral plate or sliding-hip-screw application may require distal extension and anterior elevation of vastus lateralis.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Choose table and positioning to preserve AP and lateral imaging before draping, especially when fracture fixation is planned.

closure.text: Repair the capsule and any released abductor or vastus lateralis attachment, then close fascia lata securely.

complications.text: Approach-related complications include abductor weakness or limp, femoral neurovascular injury from retraction, vascular bleeding, and iatrogenic femoral fracture during exposure.

bailouts.text: When visualization or femoral mobilization is inadequate, extend the defined exposure rather than applying uncontrolled retraction; convert to the procedure's planned extensile option when necessary.

questions.question: What muscular interval defines the Watson-Jones approach?
questions.answer: Tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly.
